subcategories.title: Reading Informational & Academic Texts
subcategories.description: Main Idea & Thesis Statement, Locating Explicit Factual Details, Paraphrasing, Drawing Logical Inferences

questions.question:
Read the passage below:
'Artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping modern educational methodologies. Intelligent tutoring systems can now diagnose individual student learning gaps in real time, adapting pedagogical content to accommodate varying cognitive paces. Furthermore, automated grading frameworks relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties, enabling them to dedicate greater attention to individualized mentorship.'

What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Teachers are gradually being replaced by computerized robots
options.B: Artificial intelligence is significantly transforming modern education practices
options.C: Grading frameworks are the most critical component of teaching
options.D: Students prefer learning from software rather than human mentors
options.E: Administrative duties have increased in modern institutions

questions.solution: The first sentence presents the primary thesis statement: AI is reshaping educational methodologies, which is then substantiated by adaptive tutoring and automated assessment in subsequent sentences.

questions.question:
Read the passage below:
'Artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping modern educational methodologies. Intelligent tutoring systems can now diagnose individual student learning gaps in real time, adapting pedagogical content to accommodate varying cognitive paces. Furthermore, automated grading frameworks relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties, enabling them to dedicate greater attention to individualized mentorship.'

According to the passage, how do intelligent tutoring systems assist learners?

options.B: By identifying learning gaps and adapting content to their individual pace
options.C: By eliminating the requirement for standardized examinations
options.D: By monitoring students' physical activities in the classroom

questions.solution: Explicitly stated in sentence 2: 'Intelligent tutoring systems can now diagnose individual student learning gaps in real time, adapting pedagogical content...'

questions.question:
Read the passage below:
'Artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping modern educational methodologies. Intelligent tutoring systems can now diagnose individual student learning gaps in real time, adapting pedagogical content to accommodate varying cognitive paces. Furthermore, automated grading frameworks relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties, enabling them to dedicate greater attention to individualized mentorship.'

It can be inferred from the passage that before AI automation, teachers...

options.A: Did not care about mentoring their students
options.B: Spent a substantial portion of their working hours on repetitive assessment tasks
options.C: Never experienced difficulties diagnosing student progress
options.D: Refused to adopt digital computer technology

questions.solution: The statement that automated grading 'relieves instructors of repetitive administrative duties' logically implies teachers previously spent significant time on those manual grading tasks.

questions.question:
Read the passage below:
'Artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping modern educational methodologies. Intelligent tutoring systems can now diagnose individual student learning gaps in real time, adapting pedagogical content to accommodate varying cognitive paces. Furthermore, automated grading frameworks relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties, enabling them to dedicate greater attention to individualized mentorship.'

What is the author's primary purpose in writing the passage?

options.A: To warn against the catastrophic dangers of classroom automation
options.B: To inform readers about the positive impacts of AI on educational methods
options.C: To advertise a commercial intelligent tutoring software brand
options.D: To criticize traditional teachers for their slow grading methods
options.E: To demand immediate school curriculum overhauls

questions.solution: The passage maintains an informative, balanced expository tone describing the technological advancements and educational benefits of AI.

questions.question: Which statement best paraphrases: 'Automated grading frameworks relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties'?

options.A: Teachers no longer have any work left to complete in school
options.B: Automated scoring systems free educators from monotonous evaluation tasks
options.C: Instructors refuse to grade students' homework assignments manually
options.D: Repetitive duties are preferred by computer algorithms
options.E: Administrative staff must be trained to replace classroom teachers

questions.solution: 'Relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties' is accurately restated as 'free educators from monotonous evaluation tasks'.

questions.question: The term 'pedagogical content' in the passage refers to...
questions.solution: Pedagogical relates to the theory and practice of education/teaching; hence pedagogical content means educational instruction material.

questions.question:
Read the passage below:
'Artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping modern educational methodologies. Intelligent tutoring systems can now diagnose individual student learning gaps in real time, adapting pedagogical content to accommodate varying cognitive paces. Furthermore, automated grading frameworks relieve instructors of repetitive administrative duties, enabling them to dedicate greater attention to individualized mentorship.'

Which of the following is NOT true according to the passage?

options.A: AI systems can adapt content to different learning speeds
options.B: AI tools enable teachers to provide more individualized mentorship
options.C: AI will completely eliminate the need for human teachers by next year
options.D: AI can evaluate diagnostic medical and educational patterns
options.E: Intelligent tutoring software operates in real-time

questions.solution: The text never claims AI will eliminate human teachers; on the contrary, it emphasizes that AI enables teachers to focus more on personal mentorship.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Coral reefs occupy less than 0.1 percent of the ocean's surface area, yet they harbor approximately 25 percent of all marine species. Rising sea surface temperatures disrupt the symbiotic relationship between corals and zooxanthellae algae, triggering widespread coral bleaching.'

What would most likely happen if sea temperatures continue to climb indefinitely?

options.A: Coral reefs will expand rapidly across all oceans
options.B: A catastrophic collapse of ocean biodiversity affecting a quarter of marine life
options.C: Zooxanthellae algae will begin hunting deep-sea fish
options.D: The percentage of the ocean covered by coral will reach 25 percent
options.E: Marine species will adapt immediately without any losses

questions.solution: Since 25% of marine species depend on corals and warm waters cause fatal bleaching, prolonged temperature rises would collapse that marine biodiversity.

questions.question: In an academic analytical exposition essay, the thesis statement is conventionally positioned...

options.A: In the middle of the bibliography list
options.B: At the end of the introductory paragraph
options.D: As the caption of the first illustration

questions.solution: Academic convention places the central thesis statement at or near the end of the introductory paragraph.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Coral reefs occupy less than 0.1 percent of the ocean's surface area, yet they harbor approximately 25 percent of all marine species. Rising sea surface temperatures disrupt the symbiotic relationship between corals and zooxanthellae algae, triggering widespread coral bleaching.'

Based on the passage above, what directly triggers coral bleaching?

options.B: The breakdown of the symbiotic relationship with photosynthetic algae due to warm waters

questions.solution: The passage explicitly links elevated temperatures to the disruption of symbiosis between corals and zooxanthellae, causing bleaching.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Coral reefs occupy less than 0.1 percent of the ocean's surface area, yet they harbor approximately 25 percent of all marine species. Rising sea surface temperatures disrupt the symbiotic relationship between corals and zooxanthellae algae, triggering widespread coral bleaching.'

According to the passage, what proportion of marine species relies upon coral reefs?
questions.solution: Explicit text: '...yet they harbor approximately 25 percent of all marine species.'

questions.question: When an author compares the function of a computer CPU to a human brain, what rhetorical technique is being employed?
questions.solution: An analogy explains an unfamiliar or technical concept by demonstrating its functional similarity to something familiar.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences represents an empirical FACT?

options.A: Quantum computers are undeniably the greatest human invention ever built
options.B: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure
options.C: Python is far more enjoyable to learn than any other coding language
options.D: Working remotely is undoubtedly superior to working in a corporate office
options.E: Electric cars are boring compared to vintage muscle cars

questions.solution: Sentence B is an empirically verifiable, measurable scientific fact. The others contain subjective opinion markers (*undeniably greatest, enjoyable, superior, boring*).

questions.question: The tone of a peer-reviewed academic journal article investigating vaccine efficacy is typically...
questions.solution: Scientific research papers maintain an objective, empirical, neutral, and methodologically measured tone.

questions.question: A paragraph explains that sleep deprivation causes micro-sleep episodes, slower neural reaction times, and impaired memory retention. The best summary title for this section is...

options.B: Cognitive and Physiological Consequences of Sleep Deficit
options.D: The Advantages of Midnight Coding Sessions

questions.solution: The title comprehensively encapsulates both the mental (cognitive) and bodily (physiological) repercussions of insufficient sleep.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Countries investing heavily in fiber-optic telecommunications and high-tech STEM education consistently achieve higher GDP growth than those dependent exclusively on raw mineral extraction.'

What can be reasonably concluded?

options.A: Mineral extraction should be made illegal immediately
options.B: Technological infrastructure and knowledge-based training are vital drivers of economic growth
options.C: Fiber-optic cables are made from rare minerals
options.D: Education has no measurable influence on national prosperity
options.E: All developed countries have zero natural resources

questions.solution: The correlation between STEM/fiber-optic investment and superior GDP performance demonstrates the primacy of a knowledge-based economy.

questions.question: An academic essay that presents a technical dilemma and subsequently details three methods to mitigate it follows which text structure?
questions.solution: Presenting a complication followed by mitigation techniques is the classic Problem-Solution text framework.

questions.question:
Sentence: 'Unlike renewable wind and solar energy, fossil fuel combustion generates substantial greenhouse gases that accelerate global climate change.'

What is the primary point of contrast?

options.A: The financial cost of manufacturing turbines
options.B: The emission of climate-altering greenhouse gases during energy production
options.C: The physical weight of coal versus sunlight
options.D: The geographical location of power grids

questions.solution: The contrast hinges directly on the generation of greenhouse gas emissions versus renewable clean alternatives.

questions.question: A chart shows smartphone sales rising from 200 million units in 2010 to 1.4 billion units in 2020. This indicates a...

options.B: Sevenfold increase in annual sales volume

questions.solution: 1.4 billion divided by 200 million = 7. Thus it represents a sevenfold growth.

questions.question: When taking a timed standardized reading examination, which strategy is most effective for long technical passages?

options.A: Reading each word three times slowly before looking at questions
options.B: Skimming the passage for the main thesis, reviewing questions, and scanning back for specific keywords
options.C: Translating the entire English text into Indonesian on rough paper
options.D: Guessing option C for all questions without reading
options.E: Reading only the last sentence of the entire article

questions.solution: Skimming for structure followed by targeted scanning for question keywords is the scientifically validated high-scoring reading strategy.

questions.question:
Read the instruction snippet:
'Step 3: Ensure your MySQL database service is active before running `php artisan migrate`. If connection errors occur, verify your DB_HOST and DB_PORT credentials in the `.env` file.'

What should a developer do if the migration command fails to connect?

options.B: Check DB_HOST and DB_PORT configuration values in the `.env` file

questions.solution: Explicitly instructed: 'If connection errors occur, verify your DB_HOST and DB_PORT credentials in the `.env` file.'

questions.question:
Read the instruction snippet:
'Step 3: Ensure your MySQL database service is active before running `php artisan migrate`. If connection errors occur, verify your DB_HOST and DB_PORT credentials in the `.env` file.'

According to the manual above, what prerequisite must be satisfied BEFORE running `php artisan migrate`?

options.A: The Apache web server must be uninstalled
options.B: The MySQL database service must be active and running
options.C: The user must restart their computer twice
options.D: All PHP files must be renamed to .html

questions.solution: Prerequisite stated in the manual: 'Ensure your MySQL database service is active before running...'

questions.question:
Email excerpt:
'Dear Ms. Johnson,
Thank you for considering our consulting firm. We have reviewed your architectural specifications and would like to formally request an extension until this Friday to finalize the cost estimation breakdown.'

What is the main objective of this email?

options.A: To reject the client's proposal entirely
options.B: To ask for additional time (extension) until Friday to complete the quotation
options.D: To resign from the consulting company
options.E: To invite Ms. Johnson to a holiday party

questions.solution: The core communicative act: '...formally request an extension until this Friday to finalize the cost estimation breakdown.'

questions.question:
Job advertisement:
'Position: Junior Web Developer (Laravel)
Requirements:
- Vocational High School (SMK RPL) or Bachelor's in Computer Science.
- Proven competency in PHP, Laravel framework, and MySQL database.
- Familiarity with Git version control is advantageous.'

Which candidate best matches the mandatory requirements?

options.A: An accountant with no coding background
options.B: A vocational high school RPL graduate with hands-on Laravel and MySQL skills
options.C: A graphic designer who only knows Adobe Photoshop
options.D: A civil engineer with experience in bridge maintenance
options.E: A high school student who has never written code

questions.solution: The SMK RPL graduate with Laravel and MySQL skills satisfies both education and technical proficiency requirements.

questions.question:
Job advertisement:
'Position: Junior Web Developer (Laravel)
Requirements:
- Vocational High School (SMK RPL) or Bachelor's in Computer Science.
- Proven competency in PHP, Laravel framework, and MySQL database.
- Familiarity with Git version control is advantageous.'

In the job advertisement above, what does 'Familiarity with Git version control is advantageous' imply?

options.A: Applicants without Git will be fined
options.B: Git skill is a welcome plus/benefit, though not the primary baseline requirement
options.C: Git is strictly prohibited by the company
options.D: The company does not use version control
options.E: Git is only used by senior executives

questions.solution: 'Advantageous' or 'preferred' indicates a bonus qualification that gives an applicant a competitive edge.

questions.question:
Public notice: 'Attention all passengers: Scheduled maintenance on the northbound rail line will commence at 22:00. Commuters are advised to utilize the shuttle bus service located at Exit B.'

Where should travelers go after 22:00 to continue their journey?

options.A: To Platform 1 on the train tracks
options.B: To the shuttle bus pickup area at Exit B
options.D: To the ticket refund counter at Exit A

questions.solution: Commuters are instructed to take shuttle buses stationed at Exit B during maintenance.

questions.question:
Customer service response: 'We sincerely apologize for the delayed dispatch of order #4082. A replacement unit has been shipped via priority courier at no additional charge.'

How did the company resolve the issue?

options.A: By charging the customer double the delivery fee
options.B: By sending a replacement unit via priority courier free of charge
options.C: By canceling the order permanently without notice
options.D: By offering a store coupon valid only next year

questions.solution: The company sent a replacement with expedited courier without extra fees.

questions.question:
Warning label on a laser cutter: 'DANGER: High-voltage components inside. Disconnect power cord before removing protective casing. Do not operate without safety goggles.'

What action must be performed FIRST before opening the case?

options.C: Turning the cutting power to maximum

questions.solution: The instruction specifically mandates: 'Disconnect power cord before removing protective casing.'

questions.question:
Meeting Schedule:
- 09:00 - 09:30: Welcome & Project Overview
- 09:30 - 10:45: Database Migration & API Integration
- 10:45 - 11:00: Coffee Break
- 11:00 - 12:00: UI/UX Presentation

At what time will the discussion regarding API Integration conclude?
questions.solution: The agenda slot for Database Migration & API Integration spans 09:30 to 10:45.

questions.question:
Memorandum excerpt: 'Effective immediately, all leave requests exceeding three consecutive days must be submitted through the portal at least two weeks in advance.'

If an employee plans a 5-day holiday, when must they submit their request?

options.A: On the morning of the holiday
options.B: At least two weeks prior to the intended leave date
options.C: One day after returning to work
options.D: At the end of the calendar year

questions.solution: The memo specifies: '...at least two weeks in advance' for leaves over 3 days.

questions.question:
Warranty card: 'This warranty covers manufacturer defects for 12 months. Damages caused by liquid spill, drop impact, or unauthorized tampering are strictly excluded.'

Which scenario is covered under this warranty?

options.A: The laptop screen broke after falling onto a tiled floor
options.B: Coffee spilled across the keyboard causing a short circuit
options.C: The internal motherboard failed due to a defective factory capacitor
options.D: An unauthorized repair shop replaced the battery
options.E: The user cracked the chassis with a screwdriver

questions.solution: Factory component flaws are 'manufacturer defects', which are protected, whereas drops, spills, and tampering are explicitly excluded.

questions.question: When writing a formal business inquiry to an organization where the recipient's name is unknown, the most appropriate opening salutation is...

options.B: Dear Sir or Madam, / Dear Hiring Manager,

questions.solution: 'Dear Sir or Madam,' or 'Dear Hiring Manager,' is the standard polite business salutation for unnamed recipients.

questions.question:
Changelog v2.4.0:
- Fixed CSRF vulnerability in profile upload form.
- Accelerated database querying by adding indexes to user_id.
- Deprecated legacy PHP 7.4 compatibility.

What security improvement was made in version 2.4.0?

options.B: Patched a CSRF vulnerability in the profile upload form

questions.solution: First bullet point explicitly notes: 'Fixed CSRF vulnerability in profile upload form.'

questions.question:
Flight Itinerary:
- Flight GA-402: Depart CGK Jakarta 14:15 WIB -> Arrive DPS Bali 17:05 WITA.
What is the scheduled departure time in Jakarta local time?
questions.solution: Departure is listed as 14:15 WIB from CGK Jakarta.

questions.question:
Invitation: 'We cordially invite you to the National Web Tech Summit. Please RSVP by September 15th to guarantee your seat and dietary preferences.'
What will happen if a participant registers after September 15th?

options.A: They will be fined by the organizers
options.B: Seat availability and dietary arrangements cannot be guaranteed
options.D: They must deliver the keynote address

questions.solution: The deadline exists specifically to guarantee seating and meal accommodations.

questions.question:
Bank notice: 'A service fee of Rp15,000 will be debited monthly from accounts maintaining an average balance below the minimum threshold of Rp1,000,000.'
How can an account holder avoid this fee?

options.B: By keeping their average balance at or above Rp1,000,000

questions.solution: Maintaining an average balance equal to or higher than the minimum threshold avoids the monthly penalty.

questions.question:
Safety directive: 'In the event of an earthquake, execute Drop, Cover, and Hold On under a sturdy desk. Do not use elevators under any circumstances.'
Why are elevators prohibited during an earthquake?

options.B: Risk of power disruption and entrapment inside elevator shafts
options.D: Elevators are reserved for fire drills only
options.E: It is inconvenient for security guards

questions.solution: Power outages and cable/shaft misalignment during tremors can trap occupants inside elevators.

questions.question:
API Reference:
`POST /api/v1/auth/login`
Header: `Content-Type: application/json`
Body: `{"email": "string", "password": "string"}`
Response: `200 OK -> {"token": "..."}`

What HTTP method is required to submit login credentials?
questions.solution: The documentation specifies the `POST` method for the login route.

questions.question:
Delivery receipt: 'Signature required upon delivery. If recipient is unavailable, package will be retained at the local hub for 5 business days.'
How long will the depot store the parcel before taking further action?
questions.solution: Explicitly declared: '...retained at the local hub for 5 business days.'

questions.question: Which of the following represents an acceptable formal sign-off in a professional business letter?
questions.solution: 'Sincerely yours,' and 'Best regards,' are the established polite and formal sign-offs in business writing.

subcategories.title: Vocabulary in Context & Lexical Nuance
subcategories.description: Context Clues (Definition, Contrast, Example), Word Formation (Prefixes/Suffixes), High-Frequency Academic Vocabulary

questions.question:
Sentence: 'Unlike his gregarious brother who thrived in massive social gatherings, Daniel was quite introverted, preferring quiet solitary evenings.'
What does the word 'gregarious' mean in this context?
questions.solution: The contrast signaled by 'Unlike...' juxtaposes Daniel's introversion with his brother's 'gregarious' personality, which thrived in social gatherings (sociable).

questions.question: In the sentence 'The engineering team will implement the new caching strategy next week,' the word 'implement' is closest in meaning to...
questions.solution: To implement a strategy means to execute, carry out, or put it into active operation.

questions.question: The prefix 'sub-' in words like 'subcategory', 'submarine', and 'subordinate' denotes...
questions.solution: The Latin prefix 'sub-' means under, below, or subordinate/secondary.

questions.question: Adding the suffix '-tion' to the verb 'migrate' produces 'migration', which transforms the word into a/an...
questions.solution: The suffix '-tion' creates abstract nouns denoting action or condition (*migrate -> migration, innovate -> innovation*).

questions.question: Sentence: 'Electronic component shortages account for nearly 40% of recent production delays.' What does 'account for' mean here?

options.B: Explain or constitute the cause of

questions.solution: In statistical and causal contexts, 'account for' means to represent, constitute, or explain the proportion of something.

questions.question: In the phrase 'a comprehensive syllabus covering all competition topics', the word 'comprehensive' means...
questions.solution: Comprehensive means complete, thorough, and including all essential aspects.

questions.question: The cryptocurrency market is notoriously **volatile**, whereas government treasury bonds remain remarkably...
questions.solution: 'Volatile' means rapidly changing and unpredictable; its natural antonym in financial contexts is 'stable' or 'steady'.

questions.question:
Sentence: 'The botanist discovered an **epiphyte**, a plant that derives moisture and nutrients from the air and rain and usually grows upon another plant without being parasitic.'
What type of context clue is used to define 'epiphyte'?
questions.solution: The definition is provided directly between commas immediately following the term.

questions.question: Which verb naturally collocates with the noun 'research' in formal academic writing?
questions.solution: Standard academic collocation is 'to conduct research' or 'to undertake research'.

questions.question: The prefix 'mis-' in 'misleading', 'miscalculation', and 'misconception' signifies...
questions.solution: 'Mis-' denotes bad, erroneous, or wrong action (*miscalculate = calculate wrongly*).

questions.question: In the sentence 'The students carried out the chemistry experiment meticulously,' 'carried out' is closest to...
questions.solution: To 'carry out an experiment' means to perform, conduct, or execute it.

questions.question: In computer software engineering, a 'robust architecture' is one that...

options.B: Is resilient, sturdy, and handles errors gracefully

questions.solution: In software, robust refers to resilience, reliability, and fault-tolerance under demanding conditions.

questions.question: The adjective suffix '-able' (as in 'scalable', 'maintainable', 'usable') conveys the meaning of...
questions.solution: '-able' forms adjectives indicating ability or capacity (*maintainable = capable of being maintained*).

questions.question: Sentence: 'Developers must [...] that all passwords are encrypted before database insertion.' The correct word is...
questions.solution: 'Ensure' means to make certain that something happens. 'Insure' relates to financial insurance policies, and 'assure' means to convince a person.

questions.question: Which of the following words carries a decidedly NEGATIVE connotation?
questions.solution: 'Dilapidated' means decayed, broken down, or in state of ruin (negative). The others are positive qualities.

questions.question: Sentence: 'Due to severe torrential rains, the outdoor sports festival was called off.' 'Called off' means...
questions.solution: The idiomatic phrasal verb 'call off' means to cancel.

questions.question: The word 'subsequent' is synonymous with...
questions.solution: Subsequent means happening afterward or following in sequence.

questions.question: In medical and scientific terms like 'hypertension' and 'hypersensitive', the prefix 'hyper-' means...
questions.solution: 'Hyper-' signifies over, above, or excessive (*hyperactive, hypertension*).

questions.question: Sentence: 'The chef utilized various condiments, such as mustard, mayonnaise, relish, and barbecue sauce.' The examples illustrate that condiments are...
questions.solution: Mustard, mayo, and relish are seasonings/sauces added to food to impart flavor.

questions.question: Sentence: 'The crisp salad serves as a perfect [...] to the rich steak.' The correct spelling is...
questions.solution: 'Complement' (with 'e') means something that completes or goes well with something else. 'Compliment' (with 'i') is praise.

subcategories.title: Author's Purpose, Tone & Critical Stance
subcategories.description: Identifying Author's Tone, Differentiating Fact from Opinion & Bias, Recognizing Target Audience and Rhetorical Goals

questions.question:
Passage: 'It is utterly absurd that in the twenty-first century, millions of citizens still lack access to potable drinking water while billions are squandered on corporate vanity projects.'
What is the author's tone?
questions.solution: Diction such as 'utterly absurd', 'squandered', and 'vanity projects' expresses righteous anger and indignation.

questions.question: An article detailing the configuration of Docker container networks, kernel parameters, and YAML compose syntax is primarily intended for...
questions.solution: The technical domain knowledge directly targets systems engineers, developers, and DevOps practitioners.

questions.question: A brochure that describes the features of an eco-friendly water heater, presents customer testimonials, and offers a 20% discount coupon is written primarily to...

options.B: Persuade readers to purchase the product

questions.solution: Coupons, testimonials, and feature highlights are persuasive marketing tools designed to drive sales.

questions.question: Which of the following statements reveals personal AUTHOR BIAS?

options.A: The speed limit on national highways is 100 kilometers per hour
options.B: Traditional brick-and-mortar shopping is infinitely superior to lazy online ordering
options.C: The transaction was recorded on September 4th, 2026
options.D: Water molecules consist of hydrogen and oxygen atoms
options.E: The company employs 250 full-time staff members

questions.solution: Phrases like 'infinitely superior' and 'lazy online ordering' demonstrate subjective, emotional prejudice (bias).

questions.question:
Passage: 'The startup boldly promises that their new dietary pill burns fat while you sleep with zero physical exercise. However, independent clinical evidence remains conspicuously absent.'
The author's attitude toward the startup's claim is best described as...
questions.solution: Pointing out the absence of independent verification indicates healthy scientific skepticism.

questions.question: Which sentence is written in an OBJECTIVE, UNBIASED tone?

options.A: The minister's ridiculous speech was a total embarrassment to the nation
options.B: The ministry reported that tax revenues increased by 4.2 percent in the third quarter
options.C: Only foolish people would invest in green energy technologies
options.D: The awful movie bored every single person in the cinema to tears
options.E: Our heroic team obliterated the pathetic opposition

questions.solution: Sentence B reports official quantitative data dispassionately without editorial adjectives.

questions.question: If an author repeatedly presents both the economic advantages of urban expansion and its environmental toll with equal gravity, the author's stance is...
questions.solution: Weighing positive and negative impacts with methodological parity exemplifies a balanced stance.

questions.question: When an author writes an article playfully suggesting that teenagers be forced to communicate exclusively in Morse code to reduce screen time, the author is using...

options.B: Satire / irony to make a point

questions.solution: Satire employs absurdity and humor to comment upon contemporary social phenomena.

questions.question: An encyclopedia entry defining the life cycle of a monarch butterfly is written primarily to...
questions.solution: Encyclopedic entries are informative expository texts intended to educate.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Despite past setbacks in battery chemistry, recent breakthroughs in solid-state cells promise to make affordable, zero-emission aviation a reality within our decade.'
The tone here is...
questions.solution: 'Promise to make affordable... a reality' conveys forward-looking technological optimism.

questions.question: 'Since city dwellers are glued to smartphones, public transit authorities should abandon paper timetables immediately.' What assumption does the author make?

options.A: Every single transit rider possesses a functional digital smartphone and internet data
options.B: Paper is made from recycled fibers
options.D: Smartphone batteries never run out of power

questions.solution: The recommendation presumes universal smartphone possession, cellular connectivity, and continuous battery charge among all passengers.

questions.question:
Passage: 'The abandoned playground lay silent under the grey autumn sky, its rusted swings swaying gently in the lonely wind, echoing memories of children long grown and departed.'
The prevailing tone is...
questions.solution: Images of rust, autumn grey, silence, and departed youth evoke nostalgic melancholy.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an exaggerated HYPERBOLIC assertion?

options.A: The library closes at 20:00 on weekdays
options.B: I have told you a billion times to back up your database before running migrations!
options.C: The server response latency was measured at 120 milliseconds
options.D: The conference takes place in Singapore next month
options.E: Three new pull requests were merged into the main branch

questions.solution: 'Told you a billion times' is a figurative, exaggerated hyperbole.

questions.question: In a speech, repeating the phrase 'We shall not falter; we shall not surrender; we shall not yield' serves to...

options.B: Emphasize resolute determination and inspire emotional conviction

questions.solution: Anaphora (rhetorical repetition at the start of clauses) powerfully intensifies emotional resolve and persuasion.

questions.question: In a debate on nuclear power, an author who highlights zero carbon emissions while dismissing nuclear waste management concerns is demonstrating...
questions.solution: Highlighting advantages while deliberately omitting major counterarguments constitutes one-sided bias.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Immediate evacuation of coastal zones is mandatory. The category 5 cyclone is projected to make landfall within three hours with catastrophic storm surges.'
What is the tone?
questions.solution: Directives like 'mandatory', 'immediate', and 'catastrophic' project life-saving urgency.

questions.question: After winning a national gold medal with a flawless score of 100, the contestant remarked: 'I suppose I did okay.' This remark is an example of...
questions.solution: Deliberately minimizing a stellar achievement is classic rhetorical understatement (litotes).

questions.question: A passage written explicitly to instruct readers on moral rectitude and civic duty is described as...
questions.solution: Didactic literature intends to instruct or impart ethical/moral lessons.

questions.topic: Author Point of View in Argument
questions.question: If an editorial asserts 'We must hold our municipal council accountable for polluted waterways,' the pronoun 'We' functions to...

options.A: Create solidarity and shared civic responsibility between author and readers

questions.solution: The inclusive 'We' fosters collective civic solidarity between writer and readership.

questions.question: A report presenting data on rising childhood obesity should conclude by...

options.A: Recommending actionable nutritional and physical activity interventions

questions.solution: A well-structured academic health report concludes with targeted, actionable public policy and lifestyle recommendations.

subcategories.title: Discourse Cohesion & Text Organization
subcategories.description: Transitional Signals (Contrast, Cause, Addition), Pronoun Reference, Paragraph Structure & Sentence Insertion

questions.question:
Sentence: 'The software passed all automated unit tests. [...], several critical bugs were uncovered during live beta testing with real users.'
The most appropriate transitional signal is...
questions.solution: 'However' or 'Nevertheless' introduces an unexpected contrast to the preceding sentence about passing automated tests.

questions.question:
Sentence: 'The server experienced an unprecedented distributed denial-of-service attack. [...], the administration temporarily suspended all inbound external traffic.'
The best connector is...
questions.solution: Suspending external traffic was the direct consequence of the attack; 'Therefore' or 'As a result' expresses this causal link.

questions.question:
Passage: 'Researchers synthesized a novel titanium alloy and compared it with standard carbon fiber. **It** exhibited remarkable resilience under high temperatures.'
What does the pronoun '**It**' refer to?
questions.solution: 'It' is the grammatical subject following the comparison, referring back to the primary subject 'a novel titanium alloy'.

questions.question:
Sentence: 'Regular cardiovascular exercise strengthens the heart muscle. [...], it stimulates the release of endorphins that reduce anxiety.'
Which linker best indicates addition?
questions.solution: 'Moreover' or 'Furthermore' adds a complementary positive health benefit to the previous point.

questions.question:
Sentence: '[...] the heavy monsoon downpour, the construction team completed the bridge ahead of schedule.'
The correct grammatical choice is...
questions.solution: 'The heavy monsoon downpour' is a noun phrase without a finite verb. Prepositions like 'Despite' or 'In spite of' precede noun phrases, whereas conjunctions (*Although, Even though*) require a full clause.

questions.question: Paragraph 1 outlines the theoretical principles of blockchain cryptography. Paragraph 2 details specific vulnerabilities encountered when implementing smart contracts. The relationship between Paragraph 1 and 2 is best described as...

options.A: Paragraph 2 repeats Paragraph 1 word for word
options.B: Paragraph 2 presents practical complications and limitations of the concept introduced in Paragraph 1
options.D: Paragraph 2 provides a biography of the author
options.E: Paragraph 2 is entirely unrelated to Paragraph 1

questions.solution: Paragraph 2 shifts from theoretical ideals to practical operational pitfalls.

questions.question: Where should the sentence 'Such unprecedented measures, however, drew sharp condemnation from civil liberties advocates' be inserted in an article?

options.A: Immediately after a sentence describing the drastic emergency restrictions implemented by authorities
options.B: At the very beginning of the introductory paragraph
options.C: Inside a footnote explaining a Latin word
options.D: Before the title of the article

questions.solution: The demonstrative phrase 'Such unprecedented measures' requires an immediately preceding sentence that specifies those drastic measures.

questions.question:
Sentence: 'Solar, wind, and geothermal power require substantial upfront capital. Nevertheless, **these** generate zero operational carbon emissions.'
'**These**' refers to...
questions.solution: 'These' plural demonstrative pronoun refers to the renewable energy sources enumerated in the first clause.

questions.question: To introduce specific illustrative evidence supporting a broad claim, which discourse marker is most suitable?
questions.solution: 'For instance' and 'For example' introduce concrete evidentiary illustrations.

questions.question: Which transitional phrase appropriately signals the final synthesis or summary of an essay?
questions.solution: 'To sum up' or 'In conclusion' alerts readers that the text has entered its concluding synthesis.

questions.question: In narrative and process descriptions, words like 'initially', 'subsequently', 'meanwhile', and 'ultimately' establish...
questions.solution: These adverbs denote progression across time (temporal order).

questions.question: Sentence: 'I wanted to purchase an ultra-wide monitor, but there were no good **ones** in stock.' The word '**ones**' substitutes for...
questions.solution: 'Ones' is an anaphoric substitute pronoun replacing the repeated noun 'ultra-wide monitors'.

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly punctuated when using 'however' as a conjunctive adverb between two independent clauses?

options.A: The flight was delayed however we arrived on time.
options.B: The flight was delayed; however, we arrived on time.
options.C: The flight was delayed, however we, arrived on time.
options.D: The flight, was delayed however; we arrived on time.
options.E: The flight was delayed however; we arrived, on time.

questions.solution: When joining two independent clauses, a conjunctive adverb requires a semicolon before it and a comma after it: `; however,`.

questions.question: Sentence: 'The developer evaluated both Vue and React. She ultimately selected **the latter** for its extensive corporate ecosystem.' Which framework was selected?
questions.solution: 'The former' refers to the first of two (Vue); 'the latter' refers to the second mentioned item (React).

questions.question: Repeating the core term 'cybersecurity' across successive paragraphs serves to...

options.B: Maintain thematic thread and lexical cohesion throughout the discourse

questions.solution: Lexical reiteration anchors readers to the central subject across complex argumentative shifts.

questions.question: Sentence: '[...] the server receives a valid cryptographic token, API access will be denied.' The appropriate word is...
questions.solution: 'Unless' means 'if not'. Sentence meaning: 'If the server does NOT receive a valid token, access will be denied.'

questions.question: Which phrase is used to rephrase or clarify a preceding statement in more accessible terms?

options.A: In other words / That is to say

questions.solution: 'In other words' signals an explanatory rephrasing for clarity.

questions.question: A paragraph begins with: 'Modern web frameworks streamline backend development.' The most logical next sentence is...

options.A: Dinosaurs went extinct millions of years ago
options.B: For example, Laravel automates routine tasks such as authentication, database migrations, and routing
options.C: Cooking pasta requires boiling salted water
options.D: The Moon revolves around the Earth

questions.solution: Sentence B provides the concrete specific example (Laravel) directly illustrating the broad opening assertion.

questions.question: A cohesive chain composed of 'developer -> programmer -> software engineer -> coder' is an example of...
questions.solution: These terms are semantic synonyms referring to the same professional role.

questions.question: Which of the following is a grammatically INCOMPLETE sentence fragment?

options.A: Although the team worked around the clock to finish the project.
options.B: The team worked around the clock to finish the project.
options.C: Working around the clock, the team finished the project.
options.D: Did the team finish the project?
options.E: The project was finished ahead of schedule.

questions.solution: Clause A begins with the subordinating conjunction 'Although' without any accompanying main/independent clause, making it a dependent fragment.

subcategories.title: Applied Grammar & Sentence Mechanics
subcategories.description: Tenses & Subject-Verb Agreement, Passive Voice & Reduced Relative Clauses, Conditionals & Modals

questions.question: Sentence: 'The collection of rare antique books [...] auctioned yesterday.' The correct verb form is...
questions.solution: The head noun of the subject is 'The collection' (singular). The prepositional phrase 'of rare antique books' does not alter the singular agreement: 'was auctioned'.

questions.question: Sentence: 'She [...] for this technology company since she graduated from university in 2022.' The correct verb is...
questions.solution: Action starting in the past and continuing to the present signaled by 'since + time point' requires Present Perfect: 'has worked' or 'has been working'.

questions.question: Sentence: 'If I [...] more spare time, I would contribute to open-source software repositories.' The correct form is...
questions.solution: Second Conditional (hypothetical present): If + Past Simple, would + V1. The past of have is 'had'.

questions.question: Sentence: 'If the backup server had been configured properly, the data loss [...] during the power outage.'
questions.solution: Third Conditional (hypothetical past regret): If + Past Perfect (`had been`), would have + V3 (`would not have happened`).

questions.question: Active: 'The technician is inspecting the fiber-optic cables right now.' Passive: 'The fiber-optic cables [...] right now.'
questions.solution: Present Continuous passive requires: am/is/are + being + V3 (`are being inspected`).

questions.question: Sentence: 'The engineer [...] beside the server rack is the lead network architect.'
questions.solution: Reduced relative clause of 'who is standing': the active participle '-ing' (`standing`) functions as a concise adjective phrase modifying 'The engineer'.

questions.question: Sentence: 'The software update [...] yesterday fixed several critical vulnerabilities.'
questions.solution: Reduced relative clause of 'which was released': the passive past participle `released` modifies 'The software update'.

questions.question: Sentence: 'The senior programmer [...] you interviewed this morning has accepted our job offer.'
questions.solution: The pronoun functions as the grammatical object of the verb 'interviewed' (you interviewed HIM/HER), thus requiring the objective relative pronoun `whom`.

questions.question: Sentence: 'We selected the designer [...] portfolio demonstrated extraordinary typography and UI finesse.'
questions.solution: Possessive relative pronoun denoting ownership ('the designer's portfolio') is `whose`.

questions.topic: Modal of Past Deduction 'Must Have + V3'
questions.question: Sentence: 'The office lights are off and the front gates are locked. The staff [...] home.'
questions.solution: 'Must have + V3' conveys near-certain logical deduction regarding a completed past action based on clear physical evidence.

questions.topic: Modal of Past Regret 'Should Have + V3'
questions.question: Sentence: 'I failed the certification exam because I did not study enough. I [...] harder.'
questions.solution: 'Should have + V3' expresses regret or unfulfilled moral/practical obligation in the past.

questions.question: Sentence: 'Neither the team manager nor the software developers [...] satisfied with the client's revised deadline.'
questions.solution: With correlatives like 'neither... nor...', the verb agrees with the closer subject. 'The software developers' is plural, so the plural verb `were` is required.

questions.question: Sentence: 'Every student and teacher in the school [...] given a digital access badge.'
questions.solution: Subjects preceded by 'every' or 'each' take a singular verb regardless of compound conjunctions: `was given`.

questions.question: Sentence: 'Developers should avoid [...] credentials directly in client-side JavaScript code.'
questions.solution: The verb 'avoid' is strictly followed by a gerund (-ing form): `avoid storing`.

questions.question: Sentence: 'The security auditor recommended that the administrator [...] all default root passwords immediately.'
questions.solution: Verbs of recommendation, demand, and insistence (*recommend, demand, suggest, insist*) trigger the subjunctive mood in the that-clause, using the base infinitive without -s: `change`.

questions.question: Sentence: 'An effective web application must be secure, responsive, and [...].'
questions.solution: Parallel grammatical series of adjectives: secure (adj), responsive (adj), and `maintainable` (adj).

questions.question: Sentence: 'This modern cloud server is capable [...] handling over 50,000 concurrent requests.'
questions.solution: The adjective 'capable' is followed by the preposition `of` + gerund: 'capable of handling'.

questions.question: Sentence: 'Rarely [...] such an elegant and computationally efficient algorithm.'
questions.solution: When a sentence begins with a negative or restrictive adverbial (*Rarely, Seldom, Scarcely, Never*), auxiliary inversion is required: `Rarely have we seen...`.

questions.question: Sentence: 'Of the two cloud providers evaluated, Amazon Web Services proved to be [...] for our high-throughput requirements.'
questions.solution: When comparing exactly two items ('of the two...'), formal grammatical convention uses the comparative degree with the definite article: `the more suitable`.

questions.topic: Used to vs Be Used to
questions.question: Sentence: 'The junior developer is not used to [...] with complex microservice architectures yet.'
questions.solution: 'Be used to' (meaning accustomed to) is followed by a gerund (-ing) or noun: `is not used to working`.
